item.title: Electrophysiology (in vivo)
item.description: In vivo electrophysiology in vivo electrophysiology is the technique of recording electrical signals from living cells (usually neurons) inside a living animal (e.g. mouse, rat , zebrafish). Listen to the electrical “Language” of the brain while it is live and functioning. Neurons communicate via electrical signals: Action potentials (Spikes) – fast (~1 ms) Local field potentials (LFP) – slow populations signals Recording is done as voltage vs time and from single neurons or groups

item.title: About
item.description: Trained as an experimentalist, I am driven by a curiosity to understand how nature reveals itself through biological systems and interactions. Alongside experimental work, I engage with chemoinformatics and computational tools—many created and freely shared by dedicated scientists—to explore biological complexity from a data-driven perspective. My research life sits at the intersection of molecular biology, structural biology, computation, and quantitative thinking in biology and medicine. I hold a PhD in Molecular and Structural Biology from UiT – The Arctic University of Norway, and I have worked across both experimental and computational domains.

item.title: Research
item.description: Research overview My research focuses on understanding biological systems at the interface of molecular biology, ion channel physiology, and computational analysis.I am particularly interested in how molecular mechanisms translate into cellular and physiological outcomes, and how data-driven approaches can accelerate discovery.
